visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately depicts circles sharing a common tangency point and correctly shades the region between radii 1 and 2 with the matching area formula, whereas Lesson 2 shows only many cropped tangent circle outlines with no visible shaded alternating regions and even has imperfect rendered mathematical text.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a well-formed fill-in gate with prompt, accepted answer, hint, and success feedback wired after an existing act, while Lesson 1’s quiz is basically functional but has empty explanations and references a wrong-path act that does not exist in the plan.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 uses clear, natural spoken math with good pacing, while Lesson 2 contains many raw or awkward math notations and symbols such as “2n .”, “k=1”, “n(n+1)/2”, equals signs, and “*pairs*” that would be read unnaturally or verbatim.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 generally stages visual changes closer to the narrated references with incremental cues, while Lesson 1 more often fires broad visuals at the start of lines before the narration reaches them or lacks a cue when a new result is described.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 is equally mathematically correct but more self-contained and explicit in its derivations and in clarifying that n is half the number of circles, while Lesson 2 has a helpful example-first sequence but relies more on unspecified visual actions and never clearly states the final general ring formula in narration before using it.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is more polished with cleaner centered title text and a balanced mid-lesson layout with legible diagram/equations, while Lesson 2 has visible raw LaTeX, video controls in the screenshots, an off-center/cropped diagram, and large unused empty space.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner. Four of the six dimension agents preferred Lesson 1, including very high-confidence wins in visual accuracy, narration quality, and polish, plus a solid win in conceptual accuracy. Lesson 2’s advantages were limited to interactivity and synchronization, both with moderate confidence. Weighted by confidence, Lesson 1’s strengths substantially outweigh Lesson 2’s, especially because its visuals, narration, mathematical presentation, and overall finish are more accurate and polished.
